B. $\sin\left(\frac{x}{2} +\frac{\pi }{12}\right)$
C. $\sin\left( zx-\frac{7\pi }{12}\right)$
D. $\sin\left( zx+\frac{\pi }{12}\right)$
Explanation: When the x-coordinate of the points on the graph of y = f(x) is halved and the y-coordinate remains unchanged, it is equivalent to replacing x with x/2 in the original function. This results in the function y = f(x/2). 

After shifting the obtained curve to the right by π/3 units, we can replace x with (x + π/3) in the function. Therefore, the function becomes y = f((x + π/3)/2) = f(x/2 + π/6).

Since the function y = sin(x - π/4) has the same graph as y = sin(x + π/4) shifted to the left by π/4 units, we can replace x - π/4 with x + π/4 to get x = x + π/4 + π/4. 

Therefore, the correct answer is f(x) = sin((x/2 + π/6) - π/4) = sin((x/2) - π/12 + π/6) = sin((x/2) - π/12 + π/12 + π/12) = sin((x/2) + π/12).
